svg.title: A nurse is caring for a client in the second stage of labor. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
svg.desc: No single pushing position is right for the whole second stage, and staying in one is what stalls descent. Squatting opens the pelvic outlet, hands-and-knees helps a baby rotate out of occiput-posterior, and side-lying slows a rapid descent — so the nurse encourages frequent changes. Holding the breath for 10 seconds is coached Valsalva pushing: it raises intrathoracic pressure, drops venous return and cardiac output, and reduces placental perfusion. Open-glottis pushing is taught instead. Maternal vital signs are taken every 5–30 min in the second stage, not hourly. Once she is fully dilated and pushing she is not walked to the bathroom — she may deliver there and may not be safe to stand; the bladder is emptied by straight catheter if needed.

g.text: A nurse is caring for a client in the

following actions should the nurse take?
Encourage the client to change positions
No single pushing position is right for
the whole second stage, and staying in one
